summary: Source review finds identity-bound atomic invitation claims, strict role separation, bounded field validation, and no cross-account learner permissions. Actual emulator verification and live activation are separate pending gates.

findings.check: Resource exhaustion and trusted member boundary
findings.issue: Document sizes and owner queries are bounded, but rules cannot enforce a global request-rate limit. Approved accounts can create many records in their own namespace; verified uninvited accounts can submit one join request per identity.
findings.recommendation: Retain private invitations and revocable approved membership; monitor the Spark quota. Do not advertise this as unrestricted public registration or claim comprehensive abuse prevention.

reviewed: Create and update cannot add familyOwner or change a protected owner grant.
Only server-managed approved familyOwner grants authorize invitation management.
Self-enrollment requires exact verified Google email and an enabled unclaimed invitation; both claim and plain admission must commit together.
Existing blocked accounts cannot create replacement admission; claimed invitations cannot be reset or reused.
Invitation lists are owner-only, bounded; members can get only their own matching invitation.
Existing UID-scoped profiles, immutable events and deletion barriers remain intact.
